","char_count":804,"fact_ids":[],"source_anchors":[]},{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":3,"domain":"Illinois road signs shapes regulatory","heading":"C — road signs shapes regulatory","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Illinois road signs shapes regulatory

FACT_ID: sec12-F01 | anchor: A01
Road signs include regulatory, warning and guide categories, distinguished by shapes and colors, and the written examination asks applicants to identify them. [A01]
Why it matters: group Sign categories; recall cue Shape and color help identify sign category.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-F02 | anchor: A01
A red sign with eight sides requires a full stop at the line, otherwise before the crosswalk or, if neither exists, before the intersection, followed by yielding to pedestrians and approaching traffic. [A01]
Why it matters: group Stop signs; recall cue Octagonal red stop requires full stop and yield.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-F03 | anchor: A01
Treat a temporary stop sign erected by highway authorities like a permanent stop sign. [A01]
Why it matters: group Stop signs; recall cue Temporary stop sign still controls traffic.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-F04 | anchor: A01
For a handheld stop sign, remain stopped until the authorized crossing guard or work-zone flagger indicates it is safe to go. [A01]
Why it matters: group Stop signs; recall cue Handheld stop waits for authorized release.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-F05 | anchor: A01
The red-and-white three-sided yield sign requires letting vehicles and pedestrians proceed first. [A01]
Why it matters: group Yield signs; recall cue Triangular yield gives priority.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-F06 | anchor: A01
A round yellow railway-warning sign uses a black crossed symbol and railway letters to warn that tracks cross the road ahead. [A01]
Why it matters: group Warning shapes; recall cue Round yellow sign warns of tracks ahead.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-F07 | anchor: A01
A rural railway advance-warning sign can stand as far as seven hundred fifty feet before the crossing; slow, look, listen through an open window and stop for an approaching train. [A01]
Why it matters: group Rail warning; recall cue Advance rail sign is before the tracks.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-F08 | anchor: A01
A diamond warning sign can be yellow, yellow-green or orange with black text or symbols and calls for slower, careful driving near possible hazards. [A01]
Why it matters: group Warning shapes; recall cue Diamond shape warns of hazards.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec12-F09 | anchor: A02
A five-sided yellow or yellow-green sign with black children symbols identifies a school zone or school crossing. [A02]
Why it matters: group School signs; recall cue Five sides signal school area.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F10 | anchor: A02
A school sign depicting children with a downward arrow marks the crossing itself, while the children symbol without that arrow warns of a nearby school. [A02]
Why it matters: group School signs; recall cue Downward arrow locates school crossing.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F11 | anchor: A02
A yellow, black-lettered three-sided no-passing sign stands on the left of a two-lane two-way road where the no-passing area begins. [A02]
Why it matters: group No-passing signs; recall cue Left-side pennant starts no-passing zone.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F12 | anchor: A02
Square and rectangular shapes can serve either regulatory or guide purposes. [A02]
Why it matters: group Sign categories; recall cue Rectangle alone does not define sign purpose.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F13 | anchor: A02
Red regulatory signs such as stop, yield, wrong-way and do-not-enter signs must be obeyed. [A02]
Why it matters: group Sign colors; recall cue Red commonly gives regulatory control.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F14 | anchor: A02
Black-and-white signs can be regulatory controls or route markers. [A02]
Why it matters: group Sign colors; recall cue Black and white has more than one use.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F15 | anchor: A02
Yellow warning signs identify road conditions or dangers ahead. [A02]
Why it matters: group Sign colors; recall cue Yellow warns of conditions ahead.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F16 | anchor: A02
Yellow-green warnings can identify pedestrian and bicycle crossings, playgrounds, school-bus stops and school zones. [A02]
Why it matters: group Sign colors; recall cue Yellow-green highlights people and school hazards.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F17 | anchor: A02
Orange usually warns of construction or maintenance dangers along a road. [A02]
Why it matters: group Sign colors; recall cue Orange warns of road work.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F18 | anchor: A02
Green guide signs provide location, direction and distance information. [A02]
Why it matters: group Sign colors; recall cue Green guides travel.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec12-F19 | anchor: A03
Blue guide signs identify services along the road. [A03]
Why it matters: group Sign colors; recall cue Blue identifies roadside services.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec12-R01 | anchor: A01
Brown signs identify parks and recreation. [A01]
Why it matters: group Sign colors; recall cue Brown identifies recreation.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec12-R02 | anchor: A01
Pink signs may warn of unplanned incidents such as crashes or natural disasters. [A01]
Why it matters: group Sign colors; recall cue Pink can mark incident hazards.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec12-R03 | anchor: A01
A regulatory sign gives a direction that drivers must obey. [A01]
Why it matters: group Regulatory controls; recall cue Regulatory instructions are mandatory.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec12-R04 | anchor: A01
At an all-way stop, every approach stops and the first driver stopped proceeds first while the others wait their turns. [A01]
Why it matters: group All-way stops; recall cue All approaches stop, first stopped goes first.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec12-R05 | anchor: A01
Approaching a yield sign requires slowing to a safe speed and stopping when necessary before giving way to vehicles and pedestrians. [A01]
Why it matters: group Yield signs; recall cue Yield may require full stop.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec12-R06 | anchor: A01
A do-not-enter sign forbids entering the indicated road or ramp, including a wrong-direction expressway entrance. [A01]
Why it matters: group Do-not-enter signs; recall cue Do not enter the prohibited approach.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec12-R07 | anchor: A02
A speed-zone-ahead sign warns that a change of speed may soon be required. [A02]
Why it matters: group Speed signs; recall cue Prepare for approaching speed zone.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec12-R08 | anchor: A02
Posted freeway limits can specify minimum and maximum speeds, and traveling below the minimum is unlawful unless safety requires it. [A02]
Why it matters: group Speed signs; recall cue Minimum speed has safety exception.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec12-R09 | anchor: A02
A wrong-way sign warns that the vehicle is traveling against the permitted direction, such as after entering a ramp or one-way road incorrectly. [A02]
Why it matters: group Wrong-way signs; recall cue Wrong way means wrong direction of travel.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec12-R10 | anchor: A02
A red circle crossed diagonally from upper left to lower right means the depicted action is forbidden. [A02]
Why it matters: group Prohibitory symbols; recall cue Red diagonal circle prohibits depicted action.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec12-R11 | anchor: A02
A no-U-turn restriction at a divided-road opening reserves that crossing for authorized vehicles such as police, emergency or maintenance vehicles. [A02]
Why it matters: group Turn restrictions; recall cue Median opening may be for authorized vehicles only.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec12-R12 | anchor: A02
A no-right-turn or no-left-turn sign prohibits turning in its indicated direction. [A02]
Why it matters: group Turn restrictions; recall cue Prohibited turn follows shown direction.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec12-R13 | anchor: A03
On a one-way street or driveway, travel only in the direction indicated by the sign’s arrow. [A03]
Why it matters: group Direction signs; recall cue Follow one-way arrow.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec12-R14 | anchor: A03
A two-way-left-turn-lane sign identifies a shared center turn lane marked with yellow lines and white arrows. [A03]
Why it matters: group Center turn lane; recall cue Center turn lane has signs and markings.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec12-R15 | anchor: A03
A no-turn-on-red sign prohibits a right turn on red and the otherwise permitted one-way-to-one-way left turn on red. [A03]
Why it matters: group Turn restrictions; recall cue No-turn-on-red removes red-turn permission.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec12-R16 | anchor: A03
An approaching-divided-highway sign warns that a median separates opposing directions on the road being crossed or entered. [A03]
Why it matters: group Divided-road approach; recall cue Approach sign warns of divided road.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec12-R17 | anchor: A03
At an island, median or central obstruction, a keep-right sign requires using the side identified by its arrow. [A03]
Why it matters: group Keep-right signs; recall cue Pass obstruction on indicated side.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec12-R18 | anchor: A03
A slower-traffic-keep-right sign directs vehicles moving below the normal traffic speed to the right lane on the multilane road. [A03]
Why it matters: group Keep-right signs; recall cue Slower traffic uses indicated right lane.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]
